samples.question: On the left is a board of 3 by 3 square cells. Number the cells 1 to 9 in reading order: 1, 2, 3 across the top row, 4, 5, 6 across the middle row, and 7, 8, 9 across the bottom row. Eight of the cells hold a coloured tile and the colours are blue, brown, green, orange, pink, purple, teal and yellow, each used exactly once. The ninth cell is plain light grey: that is the gap, and it holds no tile. One cell is marked by a red ring: the marked cell is the cell whose centre is nearest to the centre of that red ring, and the ring is only a marker, so it neither is a tile nor changes the colour of the cell it is drawn on. On the right is a row of cream cards, each carrying one solid black triangle that points up, down, left or right. The cards are applied to the board one at a time, in order from left to right, as the grey arrow below the row shows. A card's triangle points the way the gap moves: the gap and the neighbouring cell in that direction exchange contents, so the tile in that neighbouring cell slides into the gap and the cell it came from becomes the new gap. Up means towards the top of the board, down towards the bottom, left towards the left edge and right towards the right edge. Every card drawn is a legal move: the gap always has a neighbouring cell in the direction its card points. Nothing else moves, tiles never change colour, and the cells keep their numbers throughout. The board after the cards have been applied is not drawn anywhere. After every card has been applied in order, what does the marked cell hold? Answer with one word: the colour of the tile that is in it, or empty if the gap is in it.
